_doc: Host-anomaly rules for hosts.py (nightly report + 15-min watcher). Edit to tune; wildcard patterns are case-insensitive ES wildcards on keyword fields.
_doc_net: Host network rules: suspicious_ports = outbound to Internet on these ports is Investigate; quiet_procs = path prefixes exempt from 'new destination' (rotating CDN/update traffic). Shell/interpreter/netcat or temp-path binaries reaching the Internet are always Investigate.
_doc_trusted_scripts: trusted_script_dirs: fnmatch globs matched against an interpreter's working directory / script args (from the Defend exec event). Network events of such processes are dropped from host network analysis - netmon's own collectors (feeds, RDAP, UniFi API) otherwise raise 'interpreter opened an Internet connection'.
_doc_trusted: trusted_tool_paths: fnmatch globs for known tools installed in hidden dirs (e.g. LM Studio, AI tools). They skip the temp/hidden-path and interpreter-to-Internet rules but are still covered by cmdline, service-parent, new-exec, binary-hash-change, MHR, threat-feed and new-destination rules.
_doc_service: service_parents: regexes on process.parent.executable for network/AI services; a child matching service_child_suspicious (shell, downloader, netcat...) is Investigate - the main sign of an exploited inference API, MCP tool or web app. a local AI agent running as plain python is deliberately NOT a service parent: it runs shells by design.

osquery._doc: osq.py rules for pack netmon-host-posture (osquery_pack.json). host_exceptions: host -> {posture item: reason} marks an accepted risk as ok.

risky_exposed_ports.1234: LM Studio API on the LAN (no auth by default)
risky_exposed_ports.11434: Ollama API on the LAN (no auth)

kernel.yama.ptrace_scope.why: any process can ptrace same-user processes

_doc_endpoint_ips: Maps an endpoint (Elastic Agent) host name to its LAN IP so host findings are tied to the right device for per-device alert subscriptions, risk scoring and the network map.
_doc_example: Template: copy to host_policy.json and adapt admin_sources, trusted paths and host_exceptions to your hosts.
_doc_admin_sources: Machines (IP or IP prefix -> label) that are expected to log in to your hosts and administer them. A first-seen login or failed login from a source in this list is Review; from an unlisted internal or external source it is Investigate. Put your admin workstations and jump hosts here.
_doc_failure_threshold: Number of failed logins from one internal source on one host, within the analysed window, before it is reported (default 8). Failures from an internet address are always reported regardless of this number. Lower = more sensitive.
_doc_agent_stale_minutes: Minutes without a check-in before an Elastic Agent is reported as not checking in (default 30). Raise it for laptops that sleep; lower it for servers you want to know about quickly.
_doc_silent_min_prev: A host is reported as 'stopped sending syslog' when it sent 0 events in this window but at least this many in the previous one (default 50). The minimum stops hosts that are normally quiet from alerting.
_doc_ack_days: How many days an acknowledged host finding stays quiet (default 14). After that the finding comes back if the condition still exists, so accepted risks are re-reviewed.
_doc_package_processes: Process names of package managers and system updaters (apt, dnf, buildah, podman...). Executables or file changes they cause are treated as expected software installs, not suspicious activity.
_doc_exec_allow_prefixes: Path prefixes of programs that may run for the first time without a 'new executable' finding (for example your own deploy directory). Empty by default.
_doc_memfd_allow: Programs allowed to run code from anonymous memory (memfd_create), which malware uses to avoid touching disk. Browsers and some runtimes do it legitimately; list their path prefixes here.
_doc_suspicious_exec_dirs: Directories where a running program is suspicious because normal software is not installed there (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm...). Executing from one is reported as Investigate.
_doc_suspicious_cmdline: Regular expressions (case-insensitive) matched against process command lines to catch reverse shells and download-and-run one-liners (/dev/tcp/, bash -i, nc -e, base64 -d | sh...). A match is Investigate. Invalid regexes are rejected when saving.
_doc_sensitive_paths: Files whose modification should be reported (SSH authorized_keys, sudoers, passwd/shadow, cron...). Wildcard patterns, case-insensitive; * matches any characters. Changes by package managers are marked as such.
_doc_syslog_patterns: Kernel and system log messages worth alerting on. Each entry: name -> q (an Elasticsearch wildcard matched against the message, * = anything), sev (Investigate or Review) and watch (true = also checked by the 15-minute watcher, not only the nightly run). Add a pattern to catch a message you care about.
_doc_net_suspicious_ports: Outbound connections to the internet on these ports (common backdoor, IRC, Tor and C2 ports such as 4444, 6667, 9001, 31337) are reported as Investigate.
_doc_net_quiet_procs: Programs whose connections to new destinations are not reported (browsers and updaters talk to constantly changing CDN addresses). Path prefixes. Shells, interpreters and temp-path binaries reaching the internet are still always reported.
_doc_net_interpreter_ok: Per host: interpreter programs (python, node...) whose internet web traffic is expected on that host, so 'interpreter opened an internet connection' is not raised. Format: host -> list of executable path prefixes. Empty = none expected.
_doc_trusted_tool_paths: Glob patterns for known tools installed in hidden directories (Hermes, LM Studio...). They skip the temp/hidden-path and interpreter-to-internet rules but are still covered by command-line, new-executable, hash-change and threat-feed rules.
_doc_trusted_script_dirs: Glob patterns for working directories / script paths of your own automation. Network events from processes running there are dropped from host network analysis, so netmon's own collectors do not raise alerts.
_doc_service_parents: Regular expressions for executables of network or AI services (web servers, databases, inference APIs). If such a program starts a shell or downloader (see service_child_suspicious), that is Investigate: the main sign of an exploited service.
_doc_service_child_suspicious: One regular expression naming child programs that a service should never start: shells, curl/wget, netcat, socat, telnet, base64... Used with service_parents.
_doc_package_managed_prefixes: Directories whose contents are owned by the OS package manager (/usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /lib...). An executable outside them is 'unmanaged'; a changed file inside them without a package update is suspicious.
_doc_osquery: Rules for the osquery host-posture pack: package_managed_prefixes, max_uptime_days (flag hosts that have not rebooted for kernel updates, default 45), risky_exposed_ports (port -> why it is risky when listening on the LAN), sysctl_expect (kernel setting -> accepted values, severity and reason), host_exceptions (host -> {posture item: reason} to accept a known risk) and the ld_preload_allow / nopasswd_allow / deleted_allow lists of accepted items.
